Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"For public buildings in Bombay, the British chose architectural styles that expressed imperial dominance and cultural prestige. The most spectacular exemplar of the Victorian Neo-Gothic style was the Victoria Terminus (VT), the headquarters and terminus of the Great Indian Peninsula Railway. Designed by the British architect F.W. Stevens, its construction began in 1878 and was completed in 1888. Characterized by high-pitched roofs, pointed stone arches, stained glass windows, and intricate carvings of gargoyles and Indian flora and fauna, VT dominated the city skyline. It was hailed as a triumphant cathedral of commerce and modern railway engineering, visually proclaiming British technological and political supremacy."
